items.title: Fable 5.2 is the best model in the world and I feel NOTHING. I'm so fucking done
items.summary:
Fable 5.2 is the best model in the world and I feel NOTHING. I'm so fucking done

It came out yesterday. I did not even run my shooter test on it.

Since July every new model built me a 3D shooter from 1 prompt. Kimi 3, Fable 5, GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5.5.
In September Opus 5.5 made a Blender scene and I asked out loud if this is AGI. I was in real shock.

Now I know the result before I press enter. A good shooter, yeah, im sure. I already have plenty of good shooters.

FrontierCode 2.0: Fable 5.2 gets 49.1%, Opus 5.5 gets 45.5%.
So what? Who cares about this?

The big demos now take over 1,000 agents and 8 days of compute. What actually changes for a dude like me with a single prompt? For me nothing changed since September.

And the timeline celebrates anyway. "This changes everything". The same thing was written about Opus 5.5 in September and about Astra before it. In a few weeks it will be written about the next one. 

I am tired of this race. Every few weeks there is a new number and a new round of hype, and I cannot name 1 thing I do differently because of it.

It makes me sad.

items.title: Anthropic has been receiving significant attention (Nov 6-8) following an independent evaluation report from METR. They'
items.summary:
Anthropic has been receiving significant attention (Nov 6-8) following an independent evaluation report from METR. They've found that their models have been improving at ~2x the previous rate on well-defined tasks (AECI benchmark: ~1.9x improvement since October 2025). The majority of this improvement is due to AI being used to aid their own R&D efforts. Employees using the flagship model internally claimed to see ~12x improvement in productivity. The release had heavy redactions.
Why this matters: This is the most explicit evidence we’ve seen of recursive improvement being done by a frontier lab. This accelerates capabilities timelines and raises safety concerns.
OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber (Nov 5) — a specialised variant of GPT-6 Astra. GPT-6 Cyber is rated as Critical within the OpenAI Preparedness Framework (previously High rating). It is only available to approved Daybreak Red customers. They have found 81 new high severity issues within Firefox. It has also contributed to creating exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities (588 novel) and has improved within its scope significantly.
Why this matters: This demonstrates how powerful dual-use cyber tools are seeing professional access. This will help improve defensive research.
OpenAI raised ~$11 billion in initial funding for a $1.25 trillion valuation (Nov 6). However this was lower than previous targets as the wider AI sector suffered a downturn.
Why this matters: This provides significant extra funding for compute and scaling. However, this demonstrates investor caution.
Thinking Machines Lab (Founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati) released Inkling 2 Small (Nov 5). This 594B parameter MoE model (17B active) focuses on agentic coding, vision and AI training automation. It has a score of 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. It is currently available on their Tinker platform and will be released as Apache 2.0 following third party safety testing (Expected soon). They have also raised ~$5B with a ~$40B valuation (Unconfirmed).
Why this matters: This means we now have a well funded new competitor with an efficient MoE model. It focuses on meta tasks to improve model development.
Other noteworthy developments (not primary): Google made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available with longer video clips (Up to 15s) and reduced pricing. NVIDIA released Dory 1.0 — a small looping language model. World models continuing to improve within Robotics/Autonomy (Niantic pivot). Improvements in agent reliability. AI auditors can catch most of the misbehaviour but have very high false alarm rates. No major AI specific laws or policies were introduced. Anthropic are continuing to prepare for their IPO with a lower valuation range. There have been previous regulatory actions in the U.S. and internationally.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: Jensen Huang says engineers should burn $250,000 of AI a year, and Apple just cut its engineers' AI budget to about $50,
items.summary:
Jensen Huang says engineers should burn $250,000 of AI a year, and Apple just cut its engineers' AI budget to about $50,000.

And Apple plans to cut it again.

Last month, some Apple engineers saw their daily AI spending cap drop from $300 to $200, Bloomberg reported. Some engineering teams could be cut to $100 a day next. Many groups outside engineering already sit at $100, and Apple has considered going as low as $25 for some of them.

In March, Jensen said on the All-In podcast that he'd be deeply alarmed if a $500,000 engineer used less than $250,000 of AI tokens in a year. He also said Dario Amodei's forecast of hundreds of billions in AI revenue was too conservative.

So Jensen's rule is simple: AI spending should run about half of what an engineer gets paid.

By my math, at about 250 workdays a year, $200 a day comes to roughly $50,000. The planned $100 cap comes to roughly $25,000.

By Jensen's rule, a $100 daily cap only makes sense for an engineer paid about $50,000 a year.

And Apple still wants its people using MORE AI. It's steering teams toward cheaper models and AI that runs on the device, and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has said Apple's internal work runs heavily on Anthropic's models.

I think Apple just showed where the real limit on the AI boom sits now: The finance department.

And that's just ONE company:

- Accenture capped Claude at $29 a month per employee on October 1, after some staff had been spending up to $1,000 a month, 404 Media reported.
- Uber burned through its entire 2026 AI budget in about 4 months, then capped AI coding tools at $1,500 a month per tool.
- Microsoft has cut allowances too, and its AI chief Mustafa Suleyman told Bloomberg that Anthropic is extremely expensive and that Microsoft wants to eventually get rid of that cost.
- Meta had internal leaderboards ranking staff by how many tokens they used, and now it has introduced token budgets.

The usage is clearly there. Uber's engineers used the tools so much they spent a full year's budget in 4 months.

So the people saying stop are the ones paying the bill.

That's a huge problem for the AI labs, for one reason: Their spending is already locked in. 

Anthropic has committed to $895 billion, mostly for computing power. OpenAI has signed more than $1.4 trillion of compute deals. And paying for all of it depends on companies spending more on AI per worker every year.

Apple, Accenture, Uber and Microsoft all pay for Anthropic's models, and Anthropic could start its IPO roadshow as early as next week. Its own filing shows revenue grew about 47% from the second quarter to the third, down from about 144% the quarter before, and price cuts took about $600 million out of revenue.

Plenty of people will say this is just housekeeping, and they have numbers:

Bloomberg says few Apple engineers ever used the full $300, so the savings may be small. Cheaper models can do the same work for less. Apple's R&D still rose 32% to $45.8 billion in fiscal 2026, partly because of AI. And more companies start using AI every month, so total spending can keep growing even with a cap on each worker.

But Jensen's pitch depends on spending per worker going UP. Apple, Microsoft, Meta, Uber and Accenture are all writing rules that push it down.

So the first question for Anthropic's roadshow should be simple: How much are its biggest customers spending per employee compared with a year ago, and how many of them have put caps in place?

Who's right about what an engineer's AI is worth, Jensen Huang or Apple's finance team?

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Đây là một bài toán tính nguyên hàm cơ bản trong giải tích.

**Nguyên hàm của x² là:**

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

**Giải thích:**

Sử dụng công thức nguyên hàm của hàm lũy thừa:
$$\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C \quad (n \neq -1)$$

Với n = 2:
$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

**Kiểm chứng:** Nếu lấy đạo hàm của kết quả:
$$\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x^3}{3} + C\right) = \frac{3x^2}{3} = x^2$$ ✓

Trong đó **C** là hằng số tích phân (vì đạo hàm của một hằng số bằng 0).

Có thể tôi giúp bạn với bài toán tích phân khác không?

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion:

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng recursion.
    
    Args:
        n: Vị trí trong dãy Fibonacci (n >= 0)
    
    Returns:
        Số Fibonacci thứ n
    """
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    else:
        return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# Ví dụ sử dụng
print(fibonacci(0))   # Output: 0
print(fibonacci(1))   # Output: 1
print(fibonacci(5))   # Output: 5
print(fibonacci(10))  # Output: 55
```

**Giải thích:**
- Nếu `n` là 0 hoặc 1, trả về chính `n` (trường hợp cơ sở)
- Nếu không, trả về tổng của hai số Fibonacci trước đó: `fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)`

**Lưu ý:** Phương pháp này đơn giản nhưng **không hiệu quả** với các giá trị `n` lớn vì nó tính toán lại cùng một giá trị nhiều lần. Để cải thiện hiệu suất, bạn có thể dùng **memoization**:

```python
def fibonacci_memo(n, memo={}):
    """
    Tính Fibonacci với memoization (lưu kết quả đã tính).
    """
    if n in memo:
        return memo[n]
    
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    
    memo[n] = fibonacci_memo(n - 1, memo) + fibonacci_memo(n - 2, memo)
    return memo[n]


# Ví dụ
print(fibonacci_memo(50))  # Nhanh hơn nhiều!
```

Hoặc dùng **dynamic programming** (lặp) để tối ưu hơn:

```python
def fibonacci_dp(n):
    """
    Tính Fibonacci bằng dynamic programming (lặp).
    """
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    
    a, b = 0, 1
    for _ in range(2, n + 1):
        a, b = b, a + b
    
    return b


print(fibonacci_dp(50))  # Nhanh nhất!
```
